title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 98 (Tribunal power to call meetings)

content.overview: Where it is impracticable to call a company meeting other than an AGM, or to hold or conduct it in the manner prescribed by the Act or articles, the Tribunal may act on its own motion or on an application by a director or a Member entitled to vote, order a meeting to be called, held and conducted as it thinks fit, and give ancillary directions. Those directions may include deeming one Member present in person or by proxy to constitute a meeting. A meeting held in accordance with the order is deemed duly called, held and conducted.
content.glance: Where it is impracticable to call a company meeting other than an AGM, or to hold or conduct it in the manner prescribed by the Act or articles, the Tribunal may act on its own motion or on an application by a director or a Member entitled to vote, order a meeting to be called, held and conducted as it thinks fit, and give ancillary directions. Those directions may include deeming one Member present in person or by proxy to constitute a meeting. A meeting held in accordance with the order is deemed duly called, held and conducted.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 98 (Power of Tribunal to call meetings of members, etc.). Where it is impracticable to call a company meeting other than an annual general meeting, or to hold or conduct it in the manner prescribed by the Act or the articles, the Tribunal may act on its own motion or on an application by any director or Member entitled to vote at the meeting. It may order a meeting to be called, held and conducted in the manner it thinks fit and give ancillary or consequential directions, including modifying or supplementing the operation of the Act or articles for the meeting. Directions may provide that one Member present in person or by proxy constitutes a meeting. A meeting called, held and conducted in accordance with the Tribunal's order is deemed duly called, held and conducted. This is a meeting-specific power; it is not a general power to order Board meetings. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Trigger and eligible applicant
sections.body: Where it is impracticable to call a company meeting other than an annual general meeting, or to hold or conduct it in the manner prescribed by the Act or articles, the Tribunal may act on its own motion or on an application by a director or a Member of the company who would be entitled to vote at the meeting.

sections.heading: Meeting order and ancillary directions
sections.body: The Tribunal may order a meeting to be called, held and conducted in the manner it thinks fit and give ancillary or consequential directions, including directions modifying or supplementing the operation of the Act or articles for calling, holding and conducting the meeting.

sections.heading: Single-member direction
sections.body: The Tribunal's directions may include a direction that one Member of the company present in person or by proxy shall be deemed to constitute a meeting.

sections.heading: Effect of compliance with the order
sections.body: A meeting called, held and conducted in accordance with the Tribunal's order is, for all purposes, deemed to be a meeting of the company duly called, held and conducted.

examples.title: Tribunal-called meetings
examples.body: Where it is impracticable to call a meeting of the company or of the board in the manner prescribed, the Tribunal may order a meeting to be called and conducted as it directs.

hypotheticals.question: A director says it is impracticable to call a company meeting under the ordinary procedure. Who may invoke section 98 and what may the Tribunal order?
hypotheticals.analysis: The Tribunal may act on its own motion or on an application by a director or a Member entitled to vote at the meeting. It may direct how the meeting is called, held and conducted and give ancillary directions, including that one Member present in person or by proxy constitutes the meeting. The provision does not state a general power to order a Board meeting.

hypotheticals.question: A meeting is called and conducted in accordance with a Tribunal order under section 98. What is its statutory effect?
hypotheticals.analysis: Subsection (2) deems the meeting duly called, held and conducted for all purposes, provided it was called, held and conducted in accordance with the order.

distinctions.title: Tribunal meeting order and penalty for default
distinctions.left: Section 98 allows the Tribunal to direct the calling, holding and conducting of an impracticable company meeting.
distinctions.right: Section 99 provides the penalty for default in holding a meeting under sections 96–98 or complying with a Tribunal direction.

rows.left: Compliant meeting deemed duly called, held and conducted
rows.right: Fine for company and every officer in default

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 98 as a general power to call Board meetings.
misconceptions.correction: The provision concerns an impracticable company meeting other than an AGM and the manner of calling, holding or conducting that meeting.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming any shareholder can apply regardless of voting entitlement.
misconceptions.correction: The application route specified by the section is a director or a Member who would be entitled to vote at the meeting.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the deemed-validity effect of a meeting held in accordance with the Tribunal's order.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (2) deems a compliant meeting duly called, held and conducted.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the current position on section 98?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Where it is impracticable to call a meeting of the company or of the board in the manner prescribed, the Tribunal may order a meeting to be called and conducted as it directs.
